```{r}
#| warning: false
# Load packages
library(probably)

# Set seed
set.seed(7)
```


Below are the results of a logistic regression analysis.
```{r}
#| warning: false
# Set parameter values
n <- 1e3
p_0 <- 0.6
or_age_dog <- 0.5
beta_0 <- log(p_0 / (1 - p_0))
beta_1 <- 0
beta_2 <- 0
beta_3 <- log(or_age_dog)
p_dog <- 0.445

# Generate data
dog <- rbinom(n = n,
              size = 1,
              prob = p_dog)
age_5 <- runif(n = n,
               min = 0,
               max = 60)
candy <- rbinom(n = n,
                size = 1,
                prob = plogis(beta_0 + beta_1 * dog + beta_2 * age_5 + beta_3 * dog * age_5))

# Logistic regression
mod_01 <- glm(formula = candy ~ dog * age_5,
              family = binomial)
summary(mod_01)
```

These are the variable definitions:

- `candy` is equal to 1 for participants who use candy as a coping mechanism
and 0 otherwise.
- `dog` is equal to 1 for participants who have a dog
and 0 otherwise.
- `age_5` is equal to age in years minus 5.
So, a participant of age 40 would have a value of 35
for this variable.

These are all possible sums of the coefficients, exponentiated:

- `exp(0) = 1`
- `exp(0.708233) = 2.03`
- `exp(-0.346741) = 0.71`
- `exp(-0.006168) = 0.99`
- `exp(-0.598946) = 0.55`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.346741) = 1.44`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.006168) = 2.02`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.598946) = 1.12`
- `exp(-0.346741 - 0.006168) = 0.70`
- `exp(-0.346741 - 0.598946) = 0.39`
- `exp(-0.006168 - 0.598946) = 0.55`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.346741 - 0.006168) = 1.43`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.346741 - 0.598946) = 0.79`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.006168 - 0.598946) = 1.11`
- `exp(-0.346741 - 0.006168 - 0.598946) = 0.39`
- `exp(0.708233 - 0.346741 - 0.006168 - 0.598946) = 0.78`


## Problem 1

    

Please provide the correct numerical value for the odds or odds ratio
in each statement.
Each is worth one point.

### Part (a)

The odds of using candy as a coping mechanism for someone who does not have
a dog and is five years old.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

2.03

Since there was a request for more in-depth solutions in the mid-semester feedback,
I've provided step-by-step solutions below.
You do not need to go through all these steps to solve the problems.
The learning objective was to be able to interpret the coefficients in logistic regression,
so my hope was that you would interpret the coefficients and then just find
those interpretations on the next page.
The purpose of the additional questions about odds was to help you check your answers
for the odds ratios.

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\text{odds}_i \\
    &= \exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_i -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_i -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_i \times \texttt{age\_5}_i \right) \\
    &= \exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (0) -0.006168 (0) -0.598946 (0) \times (0) \right) \\
    &= \exp\left(0.708233  \right) \\
    &= 2.03
\end{align*}
$$

:::

### Part (b)

The odds ratio comparing five-year-old dog owners to five-year-old
non-dog-owners.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

0.71

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\text{odds}_i}{\text{odds}_j} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_i -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_i -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_i \times \texttt{age\_5}_i \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_j -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_j -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_j \times \texttt{age\_5}_j \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (1) -0.006168 (0) -0.598946 (1) \times (0) \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (0) -0.006168 (0) -0.598946 (0) \times (0) \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741  \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233  \right)} \\
    &= \exp\left(- 0.346741  \right) \\
    &= 0.71
\end{align*}
$$

:::

### Part (c)

The odds ratio comparing 45-year-old non-dog-owners to 44-year-old non-dog-owners.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

0.99

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\text{odds}_i}{\text{odds}_j} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_i -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_i -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_i \times \texttt{age\_5}_i \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_j -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_j -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_j \times \texttt{age\_5}_j \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (0) -0.006168 (40) -0.598946 (0) \times (40) \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (0) -0.006168 (39) -0.598946 (0) \times (39) \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233  -0.006168 (40)  \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233  -0.006168 (39)  \right)} \\
    &= \exp\left(-0.006168   \right) \\
    &= 0.99
\end{align*}
$$

:::

### Part (d)

The odds ratio comparing six-year-old dog owners to six-year-old
non-dog-owners.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

0.39

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\text{odds}_i}{\text{odds}_j} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_i -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_i -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_i \times \texttt{age\_5}_i \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_j -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_j -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_j \times \texttt{age\_5}_j \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (1) -0.006168 (1) -0.598946 (1) \times (1) \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (0) -0.006168 (1) -0.598946 (0) \times (1) \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741  -0.006168  -0.598946  \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233  -0.006168   \right)} \\
    &= \exp\left( - 0.346741    -0.598946  \right) \\
    &= 0.39
\end{align*}
$$

:::

### Part (e)

The odds ratio comparing 36-year-old dog owners to 35-year-old dog owners.

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}

0.55

$$
\begin{align*}
    &\frac{\text{odds}_i}{\text{odds}_j} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_i -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_i -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_i \times \texttt{age\_5}_i \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 \texttt{dog}_j -0.006168 \texttt{age\_5}_j -0.598946 \texttt{dog}_j \times \texttt{age\_5}_j \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (1) -0.006168 (31) -0.598946 (1) \times (31) \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741 (1) -0.006168 (30) -0.598946 (1) \times (30) \right)} \\
    &= \frac{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741  -0.006168 (31) -0.598946  (31) \right)}{\exp\left(0.708233 - 0.346741  -0.006168 (30) -0.598946  (30) \right)} \\
    &= \exp\left( -0.006168 -0.598946   \right) \\

\end{align*}
$$

:::

## Problem 2

```{r}
#| label: fig-cal
#| fig-cap: "Calibration plot for analysis above."
cal_plot_breaks(.data = data.frame(truth = candy,
                                   estimate = mod_01$fitted.values),
                truth = truth,
                estimate = estimate)
```



The following questions refer to @fig-cal.
Each is worth one point.

### Part (a)

What is the probability of using candy as a coping mechanism
for someone with a fitted value of 0.25?

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}


0.75

You need to find 0.25 on the horizontal axis,
go up to the dot, and find the corresponding value on the vertical axis.

:::

for someone with a fitted value of 0.65?

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}


0.625 (give or take)

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Solution" collapse="true"}


Yes

:::
